source.title: Direct Language Model Alignment from Online AI Feedback
source.authors: Shangmin Guo; Biao Zhang; Tian-Lin Liu; Tian-Qi Liu; Misha Khalman; Felipe Llinares; Alexandre Ramé; Thomas Mesnard; Yao Zhao; Bilal Piot; Johan Ferret; Mathieu Blondel

page_placements.theme: Weak AI feedback (preference labels, density-ratio rewards, corrections, judge or peer-prediction rewards) for alignment training of a stronger policy

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether feedback from a weaker AI annotator can improve a stronger language model, but uses online preference annotation and win rates against baselines rather than weak-label supervised fine-tuning and PGR.
record.gate_note: Section 4.7 explicitly studies a PaLM 2-S policy trained with online DPO using PaLM 2-XS or PaLM 2-L as the preference annotator. The reported comparisons are against the SFT baseline and offline DPO, not against the weak annotator's task performance or a strong model trained on true labels. The paper also emphasizes that its teacher's discriminative preference-labeling task differs from the student's response-generation task.
record.test_reason: Section 4.7 trains a PaLM 2-S policy with online DPO, using preferences from the smaller PaLM 2-XS as annotator. It reports only Gemini Pro win rates against an SFT baseline and offline DPO. It never reports the weak supervisor's own performance, a strong-model ceiling, or PGR, so its results cannot show the student beating its supervisor (V1). There is no size or task sweep of weak-to-strong recovery either (V3). The authors say their setup differs from Burns et al.: the teacher does discriminative preference labelling and the student does generation. They call their method 'orthogonal' to weak-to-strong generalisation. The finding is related but is not a test of any version, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that OAIF from a weaker PaLM 2-XS teacher improved PaLM 2-S alignment, though less than a PaLM 2-L teacher. They stress that their teacher-student tasks differ from Burns et al.'s supervised setup.
record.recipe_differences: Uses online DPO on responses sampled from the current policy and LLM-produced pairwise preferences; it does not fine-tune on a fixed set of weak-model labels or calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: In the Helpfulness experiment, the reported win rates differ between PaLM 2-XS and PaLM 2-L annotators.

fits_no_version.finding: Online DPO preferences from the weaker PaLM 2-XS raised a PaLM 2-S policy to 77.36% win rate vs SFT and 59.44% vs offline DPO on Helpfulness. The stronger PaLM 2-L annotator gave 92.19% and 89.26%. All four win rates were judged by Gemini Pro.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference feedback from a weaker LLM annotator improves a stronger policy's alignment over its SFT initialisation, though less than feedback from a stronger annotator (weak-to-strong preference supervision for generation).

record.problems: The weak-teacher experiment reports Gemini Pro win rates against SFT and offline-DPO baselines, but not against the weak teacher or a strong true-label ceiling; uncertainty for these Figure 7 values is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other OAIF comparisons are not included because they do not use a weaker teacher to train a stronger student. The paper's broader annotator-size experiments in Section 4.5 do not test a stronger student against a weaker supervisor.

untested.parts: Student vs weak supervisor performance, strong ceiling, PGR: none reported.
No auxiliary-loss, ensembling or loss-variant change evaluated as a PGR gain.
No PGR across supervisor or student sizes or tasks. Section 4.5 varies annotator size with a PaLM 2-XS policy, so its annotators are the same size or larger than the policy, never weaker.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' with V1 and V3 links is overstated. No row compares the student with the weak supervisor, and the authors themselves frame the work as a different setup. Reclassified as discusses/T6, with the Figure 7 result moved to fits_no_version. No uncertainty is given for the Figure 7 values.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison with the weak supervisor's task performance, no true-label strong-model ceiling, and no PGR calculation.
The paper compares online and offline alignment methods, but does not test the listed training changes as changes to PGR.
PGR is not calculated; student-size sweeps, chess, reward modelling, representation predictors, and a broad comparison across tasks are not tested in the weak-teacher experiment.
No tests of exploiting supervisor blind spots, distribution-shift effects on weak-to-strong recovery, or correlated errors in this experiment.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are tested.

relation.reason: Section 4.7 explicitly discusses Burns et al. and distinguishes preference discrimination by the teacher from response generation by the student.

tranche.reason: Section 4.7 measures alignment gains against SFT and offline DPO, without comparing student performance with supervisor performance or measuring PGR. These results do not test a listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The four rows are method comparisons, suitable as related context rather than evidence for a claim version. Section 4.7 identifies a PaLM 2-S student, but does not specify comparator model sizes; the discussion's blanket claim that all aligned models are XS conflicts with that section.
